# Ordinary proof (DRAFT; zero credit)


## 2. Exact expressivity question and the guard
Following [1, Definition 6], L_b is at least as expressive as L_a if for every F ∈ L_a there exists H ∈ L_b such that for every model M in the common class and every world w, M,w ⊨ F iff M,w ⊨ H. The equivalent H must be chosen independently of M and w. “More expressive” means at least as expressive, with failure of the converse.

Fan's Conjecture 15 [1, printed p. 17] asserts: for every n ∈ ℕ, Lₙ₊₁ is more expressive than Lₙ. More explicitly, the strict direction requires
@ ∀n ∈ ℕ, ∃F ∈ Lₙ₊₁, ∀H ∈ Lₙ, ∃(M,w),
@                  (M,w ⊨ F) ≠ (M,w ⊨ H).
The other direction is already available: add a tautological determining input and recursively translate the remaining arguments. We disprove the displayed condition at n = 1. A single failed adjacent step refutes the universal conjecture; it does not overturn the established strictness of L₁ over L₀.

### Lemma 1 (guard identity)
For arbitrary formulas A,B in L₁ define G(A,B) = D₁(A; A ∧ B). On every pointed ternary model,
@ M,w ⊨ G(A,B)  iff
@ ∀u,v, S(w,u,v) → (M,u ⊨ A) → (M,v ⊨ A)
@                         → (M,u ⊨ B ↔ M,v ⊨ B).

Proof. Suppose G holds. If S(w,u,v) and A is true at both endpoints, agreement on A holds automatically. The consequent of the D₁ clause is agreement on A ∧ B. Since A is true at both endpoints, that is exactly agreement on B.

Conversely, assume the right side. Consider an S-pair agreeing on A. If A is true at both endpoints, restricted B-agreement yields agreement on A ∧ B. If A is false at both endpoints, both conjunctions are false and agree. These exhaust the agreeing cases. If A differs between endpoints, the D₁ antecedent imposes no requirement. Thus G holds. QED.

The guard filters the actual relation pairs; it does not demand constant truth on an entire cell in W. Two disconnected pieces of a cell may assign different truth values to B. Nor does the guard require equal values of B on crossing pairs. This distinction is essential when S_w is not a complete product relation.

The identity remains valid for loops, repeated endpoints, asymmetric relation slices and empty slices. It applies to modal A and B as well as letters: its proof uses only their endpoint truth values, with no restrictions on how those values were obtained.


## 3. Four cells and recursive elimination
Put C₁ = A ∧ C, C₂ = A ∧ ¬C, C₃ = ¬A ∧ C, and C₄ = ¬A ∧ ¬C. These cells partition W according to the two truth values. Define
@ Split(A,C;B) =
@   (G(C₁,B) ∧ G(C₂,B)) ∧ (G(C₃,B) ∧ G(C₄,B)).

### Lemma 2 (four-cell decomposition)
On arbitrary ternary frames, D₂(A,C;B) and Split(A,C;B) have the same truth value at every world.

Proof. Suppose D₂ holds and an S(w,u,v) pair lies inside one cell Cⱼ. The endpoints agree on both A and C, so they agree on B. Lemma 1 gives G(Cⱼ,B), for each j. Conversely, suppose all four guards hold. For an S-pair agreeing on A and C, choose the unique cell determined by the two truth values at u. Agreement puts v in that same cell. Its guard yields B-agreement, which is precisely the D₂ requirement. QED.

The Boolean-cell method is not claimed as new. Fan [1, Section 6.1, Proposition 16] uses such cells to eliminate finite determinacy arity over ordinary Kripke frames by formulas involving noncontingency. Goranko and Kuusisto [2, Proposition 3.3 and proof] use Boolean types in a universal-frame determinacy setting. Those results provide the partition technique. They do not themselves give this arbitrary-ternary unary definition: the ordinary-frame formulas exploit product slices, and the universal-frame formulas use their own global setting. Lemma 1 supplies the missing expression of restricted agreement without imposing either frame condition. No claim of inventing cells or the restricted-agreement semantic notion is intended.

### Theorem 3 (uniform translation)
There is a map t : L₂ → L₁ such that for all F ∈ L₂, every M and every w, M,w ⊨ t(F) iff M,w ⊨ F. Define it by recursion:
@ t(p) = p;   t(¬F) = ¬t(F);   t(F ∧ H) = t(F) ∧ t(H);
@ t(D₂(A,C;B)) = Split(t(A),t(C);t(B)).

Proof. Use structural induction on F, with induction hypotheses quantified over every world. The atomic case is immediate; the negation and conjunction cases follow from the Boolean truth clauses. At a modal node, Lemma 2 reduces the translated formula to the D₂ truth condition for t(A), t(C), t(B). For every pair u,v, the induction hypotheses replace each translated argument at both endpoints by its original argument. The resulting condition is exactly that for D₂(A,C;B). This proves the modal case and the induction. QED.

Quantifying the induction hypotheses over all worlds matters: subformulas are evaluated at u and v, not just at the original w. Thus the proof includes nested dependence formulas in determining and dependent positions; it is not merely a one-step substitution on atomic inputs.


## 4. Consequences and the published obstruction
### Corollary 4
L₂ and L₁ are equally expressive on arbitrary ternary frames. Hence Conjecture 15 is false at n = 1.

Proof. Theorem 3 supplies the missing direction. For the converse translate D₁(A;B) to D₂(⊤,A;B), recursively translating A,B; the extra agreement condition is always true. Both maps are uniform in the pointed model. Therefore strictness at this adjacent step fails. QED.

### Corollary 5 (Section 7.3)
The relativized agreement language of [1, Section 7.3] is equally expressive as L₁. Its operator O(A,B) has exactly the right-hand semantics of Lemma 1, so O(A,B) is defined by D₁(A;A ∧ B). Recursively replacing O proves the language translation, including nesting. The reverse translation is the source's own identity D₁(A;B) ≡ O(A,B) ∧ O(¬A,B). Thus the Section 7.3 strict-expressivity conjecture, including the proposed undefinability of O(p,q), fails.

This consequence uses a known semantic operator and a new-to-this-dossier definition in the unary language; it is not a proposal to rename the guard as a new semantic notion. Section 7.4's existing decomposition of relativized supervenience into relativized agreement can also be combined with Lemma 1. That further observation is not a separate campaign nomination or a separate formal endpoint here.

### Humberstone (2019), pp. 16-17
Humberstone [3] explicitly adopts the same arbitrary ternary semantics on p. 15, distinguishing it from product-frame determinacy. On p. 16 he asserts that D₂ cannot be defined from the Boolean connectives and D₁, and argues that such a definition would require one formula χ whose agreement relation equals the intersection of those for the two determining formulas. The partition observation is sound: one bivalent formula supplies at most two equivalence classes, while two formulas can distinguish four nonempty Boolean cells.

What is insufficient is the claimed necessity of that compression. The partition argument rules out replacing two determining inputs by one formula χ having exactly their joint agreement relation. It does not rule out a Boolean compound of several D₁ formulas, and it does not restrict how their dependent arguments may use the determining formulas. Split uses four separate guards; each guard's dependent argument contains its own cell. No single χ encodes the four-cell partition. Therefore the proposed necessary condition is unnecessary for general definability, and Corollary 4 corrects the stated D₂-from-D₁ undefinability assertion.

This correction concerns that specific assertion and its supporting necessity argument. It does not dispute the partition calculation, the demonstrated L₀-to-L₁ strictness, or the paper's other results. The lawful Monash repository PDF and its retrieval receipt are retained. We rely on the actual pp. 15-17 text, not a bibliographic inference about its semantics. We do not infer a claim of priority from the continued appearance of the contrary assertion in specialist literature.

from pathlib import Path
import sys,html

sys.path.insert(0,str(D/'local-deps'))

for n,f in [('Serif','/usr/share/fonts/liberation-serif-fonts/LiberationSerif-Regular.ttf'),('Bold','/usr/share/fonts/liberation-serif-fonts/LiberationSerif-Bold.ttf'),('Sans','/usr/share/fonts/liberation-sans-fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf'),('Mono','/usr/share/fonts/liberation-mono-fonts/LiberationMono-Regular.ttf'),('Unicode','/usr/share/fonts/google-noto-vf/NotoSans[wght].ttf'),('Math','/usr/share/fonts/google-noto/NotoSansMath-Regular.ttf'),('Symbols','/usr/share/fonts/google-noto/NotoSansSymbols2-Regular.ttf')]:
 pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont(n,f))

 out=''
 for c in text:
  if ord(c)<128 or ord(c) in pdfmetrics.getFont('Serif').face.charToGlyph:
   out+=html.escape(c)
  else:
   n=next((n for n in ['Unicode','Math','Symbols'] if ord(c) in pdfmetrics.getFont(n).face.charToGlyph),None)
   if n is None: raise ValueError('Missing glyph '+repr(c))
   out+='<font name="'+n+'">'+html.escape(c)+'</font>'
 return out

story=[]
for page in (D/'paper.md').read_text().split('<!-- PAGE -->'):
 if story:story.append(PageBreak())
 blocks=page.strip().split('\n\n')
 for b in blocks:
  if b.startswith('|'):
   rows=[[Paragraph(esc(c.strip()),small) for c in line.strip('|').split('|')] for line in b.splitlines()]
   t=Table(rows,colWidths=[245,245],hAlign='LEFT')
   t.setStyle(TableStyle([('VALIGN',(0,0),(-1,-1),'TOP'),('BACKGROUND',(0,0),(-1,0),colors.HexColor('#eaf0f5')),('LINEBELOW',(0,0),(-1,0),.6,colors.grey),('BOTTOMPADDING',(0,0),(-1,-1),4)]))
   story.extend([t,Spacer(1,9)])
  elif b.startswith('@'):
   for line in b.splitlines():story.append(Paragraph(esc(line.removeprefix('@ ')),eq))
   story.append(Spacer(1,6))
  else:
   for line in b.splitlines():
    sty=eq if line.startswith('@ ') else title if line.startswith('# ') else h if line.startswith('##') else s
    story.append(Paragraph(esc(line.removeprefix('@ ').lstrip('# ')),sty))
def footer(c,d):
 c.setFont('Sans',8);c.setFillColor(colors.HexColor('#526172'))
 c.drawString(52,27,'DRAFT · MathDB 334599 · zero accepted credit')
 c.drawRightString(560,27,str(d.page))

# Binary supervenience from unary supervenience on arbitrary ternary frames
DRAFT - 1 November 2026. Prepared with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex). No human authors or affiliations are asserted. Unaccepted research manuscript; zero accepted credit. Campaign count: 12/20 beyond 39 unchanged. Root alone accepts.

## Abstract
For the arbitrary ternary-frame semantics of Fan [1], every formula with two determining inputs has an equivalent formula with one determining input. The key identity is G(A,B) := D₁(A; A ∧ B): it expresses agreement on B restricted to relation pairs whose endpoints both satisfy A. Applying this identity to the four Boolean cells of two determining formulas gives a uniform translation, valid with arbitrary nesting. Consequently the n = 1 instance of Fan's Conjecture 15 is false. The same identity defines Section 7.3's relativized agreement operator and refutes the associated strict-expressivity conjecture. It also corrects the undefinability assertion in Humberstone [3, pp. 16-17]. The Boolean-cell technique is known; the contribution isolated here is its guard-definability bridge on arbitrary ternary frames. We supply a byte-preserved Lean certificate, a strict extracted replay, and an explicit trust boundary. This draft makes no priority claim.

## 1. Language, indexing and semantics
Fix a countably infinite set of propositional letters. For n ∈ ℕ, Lₙ is the least language generated by letters, negation, conjunction, and Dₙ(A₁,…,Aₙ;B), with all arguments in Lₙ. Thus n counts determining inputs; total connective arity is n + 1. In particular D₁ is a dyadic connective and D₂ is triadic. Our “binary supervenience” means two determining inputs, not a dyadic connective. We use D₁(A;B), also abbreviated D(A;B), for Fan's original supervenience operator ⇛₁. D₀ is unrelativized agreement. Boolean constants are abbreviations, for example ⊤ = ¬(p ∧ ¬p).

A model M = (W,S,V) has a nonempty set W, an arbitrary ternary relation S ⊆ W³, and V assigning a subset of W to each letter. Write S(w,u,v), or S_w uv. Atomic satisfaction is membership in V; negation and conjunction have their classical truth clauses. The modal clause is:
@ M,w ⊨ Dₙ(A₁,…,Aₙ;B)  iff
@ ∀u,v ∈ W, S(w,u,v) →
@   ((∀i ∈ {1,…,n}, M,u ⊨ Aᵢ ↔ M,v ⊨ Aᵢ)
@      → (M,u ⊨ B ↔ M,v ⊨ B)).

For n = 0 the antecedent is vacuous. No symmetry, reflexivity, transitivity, completeness of a relation slice, or finiteness is assumed. This is the semantics in [1, Definition 2 and Section 6]. Ordinary Kripke determinacy is the special case S(w,u,v) iff R(w,u) and R(w,v); that additional factorization will not be used.

Only its own temporary directory is removed. Per-command receipts record capped execution; the fresh extraction retains strict compilation, leanchecker, full audit and negative-control logs. The full dossier also contains source copies, retrieval receipts, reviewer reports, PDF QA and the source archive. REPRODUCE.md gives exact commands and the trust boundary.

### Diagnostics are not the proof
The independently written model script enumerates all local S_w slices and truth sets for A,C,B on zero through three worlds: 1, 16, 1024 and 262144 cases, totaling 263185. Zero worlds tests a vacuous slice convention, not a source pointed model. A separate enumeration compares three nested formulas and their translations on every two-world ternary frame and every three-letter valuation at both worlds: 98304 pointed comparisons. These are bounded diagnostics; Theorem 3 supplies the unbounded proof.

Finite negative controls find witnesses against replacing the guarded cells by unguarded D₁(cell;B), and against dropping each one of the four guarded cells. The replay's separate Lean negative controls reject a type-incorrect proof of False, reject sorry under warningAsError, and detect a deliberately injected local axiom with the module-origin audit. These controls demonstrate those particular checks; they do not certify arbitrary mutations, completeness of finite testing, or checker infallibility.

### Source and novelty limits
MathDB 334599's raw record and its hash are supplied. An open label and an empty solution array are not novelty evidence. Fan's arXiv v1 body was inspected, including Definitions 2 and 6, Conjecture 15, Section 6.1/Proposition 16 and Sections 7.3-7.4. The journal bibliographic counterpart is Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic 60(2) (2019), 283-309. Its body remains unread: the retained publisher response was an Incapsula challenge. No bypass or retry is claimed. Accordingly the exact refuted statement here is the arXiv conjecture under its recovered semantics; no unverified journal-text identity is asserted.

The inherited independent review and subsequent root ruling are preserved as distinct records: the reviewer held the significance/routine-adaptation gate; the root qualified novelty and regarded the guard bridge as substantive for the campaign. Neither record accepts this draft or changes the count. The current manuscript repeats no live priority clearance. The inherited dated registry checks were path/keyword screens with acknowledged truncation limits. Coverage of Yang/Väänänen, Ciardelli's thesis and older Humberstone works is incomplete; broader dependence and inquisitive-logic literature has not been exhaustively audited. Known Boolean cells receive explicit credit. No priority claim, publication, or accepted campaign credit follows from this dossier.

set_option pp.all true

set_option pp.fullNames true

run_cmd do

 let some idx := env.getModuleIdxFor? `Supervenience.literal_conjecture_false | throwError "missing module"

 for (n, ci) in env.constants.toList do
  if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some idx then
   count := count + 1
   let axs ← collectAxioms n
   let body := (ci.value? (allowOpaque := true)).isSome

import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace Supervenience

inductive Form (n : Nat) where
  | atom : Nat → Form n
  | neg : Form n → Form n
  | conj : Form n → Form n → Form n
  | dep : (Fin n → Form n) → Form n → Form n

structure Model (W : Type) where
  edge : W → W → W → Prop
  val : W → Nat → Prop

noncomputable def eval {n : Nat} {W : Type} (M : Model W) : Form n → W → Prop
  | .atom a, w => M.val w a
  | .neg f, w => ¬ eval M f w
  | .conj f g, w => eval M f w ∧ eval M g w
  | .dep a b, w => ∀ u v, M.edge w u v →
      (∀ i, eval M (a i) u ↔ eval M (a i) v) → (eval M b u ↔ eval M b v)

def unary (a b : Form 1) : Form 1 := .dep (fun _ => a) b

def gate (a b : Form 1) : Form 1 := unary a (.conj a b)

def split (a b c : Form 1) : Form 1 :=
 .conj (.conj (gate (.conj a b) c) (gate (.conj a (.neg b)) c))
       (.conj (gate (.conj (.neg a) b) c) (gate (.conj (.neg a) (.neg b)) c))

theorem gate_eval {W : Type} (M : Model W) (a b : Form 1) (w : W) :
 eval M (gate a b) w ↔ ∀ u v, M.edge w u v → eval M a u → eval M a v →
 (eval M b u ↔ eval M b v) := by
 simp only [gate, unary, eval]
 constructor
 · intro h u v huv hau hav
   have hh := h u v huv (fun _ => ⟨fun _ => hav, fun _ => hau⟩)
   tauto
 · intro h u v huv ha
   have haa := ha 0
   constructor
   · rintro ⟨hau, hbu⟩
     have hav := haa.mp hau
     exact ⟨hav, (h u v huv hau hav).mp hbu⟩
   · rintro ⟨hav, hbv⟩
     have hau := haa.mpr hav
     exact ⟨hau, (h u v huv hau hav).mpr hbv⟩

theorem split_eval {W : Type} (M : Model W) (a b c : Form 1) (w : W) :
 eval M (split a b c) w ↔ ∀ u v, M.edge w u v →
 (eval M a u ↔ eval M a v) → (eval M b u ↔ eval M b v) →
 (eval M c u ↔ eval M c v) := by
 classical
 simp only [split, eval, gate_eval]
 constructor
 · rintro ⟨⟨h00,h01⟩,h10,h11⟩ u v huv ha hb
   by_cases hau : eval M a u <;> by_cases hbu : eval M b u
   · exact h00 u v huv ⟨hau,hbu⟩ ⟨ha.mp hau,hb.mp hbu⟩
   · exact h01 u v huv ⟨hau,hbu⟩ ⟨ha.mp hau,fun h => hbu (hb.mpr h)⟩
   · exact h10 u v huv ⟨hau,hbu⟩ ⟨fun h => hau (ha.mpr h),hb.mp hbu⟩
   · exact h11 u v huv ⟨hau,hbu⟩ ⟨fun h => hau (ha.mpr h),fun h => hbu (hb.mpr h)⟩
 · intro h
   refine ⟨⟨?_,?_⟩,?_,?_⟩ <;> intro u v huv hu hv <;>
    apply h u v huv <;> tauto

noncomputable def translate : Form 2 → Form 1
 | .atom a => .atom a
 | .neg f => .neg (translate f)
 | .conj f g => .conj (translate f) (translate g)
 | .dep a b => split (translate (a 0)) (translate (a 1)) (translate b)

theorem translate_correct {W : Type} (M : Model W) (f : Form 2) (w : W) :
 eval M (translate f) w ↔ eval M f w := by
 induction f generalizing w with
 | atom a => rfl
 | neg f ih => exact not_congr (ih w)
 | conj f g ihf ihg => exact and_congr (ihf w) (ihg w)
 | dep a b iha ihb =>
   simp only [translate, split_eval, eval, iha, ihb]
   constructor
   · intro h u v huv ha
     exact h u v huv (ha 0) (ha 1)
   · intro h u v huv h0 h1
     apply h u v huv
     intro i
     fin_cases i <;> assumption

-- The strictness claim at n = 1 requires an L_2 formula without any L_1 equivalent.
-- This definition quantifies over all types of worlds and all ternary-frame models.
def StrictAtOne : Prop := ∃ f : Form 2, ∀ g : Form 1,
 ¬ (∀ (W : Type) (M : Model W) (w : W), eval M g w ↔ eval M f w)

theorem hierarchy_conjecture_false : ¬ StrictAtOne := by
 rintro ⟨f,hf⟩
 exact hf (translate f) (fun _ M w => translate_correct M f w)

def StrictStep (n : Nat) : Prop := ∃ f : Form (n + 1), ∀ g : Form n,
 ¬ (∀ (W : Type) (M : Model W) (w : W), eval M g w ↔ eval M f w)

def HierarchyConjecture : Prop := ∀ n : Nat, StrictStep n

theorem literal_conjecture_false : ¬ HierarchyConjecture := by
 intro h
 exact hierarchy_conjecture_false (h 1)

#print axioms literal_conjecture_false
end Supervenience

"""Run one command under the lane caps and write LABEL.log / LABEL.receipt.json into DIR.
Usage: python3 -I tools/capped.py DIR LABEL CWD -- CMD...
Caps: <= 2 CPUs, RLIMIT_CPU 120 s, wall 140 s, RLIMIT_AS 64 GiB, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2,
sampled (50 ms) private RSS (RssAnon+RssShmem of the process group) 6 GiB guard, and a
systemd user scope with MemoryMax=6G when available."""
import json, os, pathlib, resource, shutil, signal, subprocess, sys, time
out, label, cwd = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
assert sys.argv[4] == '--'
cmd = sys.argv[5:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
PAGE = os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE'); CPUS = sorted(os.sched_getaffinity(0))[:2]
pre = []
if shutil.which('systemd-run') and 'XDG_RUNTIME_DIR' in os.environ:
    pre = ['systemd-run', '--user', '--scope', '-q', '-p', 'MemoryMax=6G', '-p', 'MemorySwapMax=0', '-p', 'CPUQuota=200%']
    if subprocess.run(pre + ['/usr/bin/true'], capture_output=True, timeout=60).returncode != 0:
        pre = []
env = dict(os.environ, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX='2', LEAN_NUM_THREADS='1')


def rss(pgid):
    total = private = 0
    for q in pathlib.Path('/proc').glob('[0-9]*'):
        try:
            s = (q / 'stat').read_text(); f = s[s.rindex(')') + 2:].split()
            if int(f[2]) != pgid: continue
            total += int(f[21]) * PAGE
            for line in (q / 'status').read_text().splitlines():
                if line.startswith(('RssAnon:', 'RssShmem:')): private += int(line.split()[1]) * 1024
        except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError):
            pass
    return total, private


def setup():
    os.setsid(); os.sched_setaffinity(0, CPUS)
    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (120, 120)); resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (64 << 30, 64 << 30))


t0 = time.monotonic(); peak = peakp = 0; why = None
with (out / (label + '.log')).open('w') as f:
    p = subprocess.Popen(pre + cmd, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=f, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, preexec_fn=setup)
    while p.poll() is None:
        a, b = rss(p.pid); peak, peakp = max(peak, a), max(peakp, b)
        if b > 6 << 30 or time.monotonic() - t0 > 140:
            why = 'RSS' if b > 6 << 30 else 'wall'; os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL); break
        time.sleep(0.05)
    p.wait()
ru = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
r = {'label': label, 'command': pre + cmd, 'cwd': cwd, 'cpus': CPUS, 'exit': p.returncode, 'killed_reason': why,
     'wall_seconds': round(time.monotonic() - t0, 3), 'cpu_seconds': round(ru.ru_utime + ru.ru_stime, 2),
     'peak_sampled_private_rss_bytes': peakp, 'peak_sampled_total_vmrss_bytes': peak, 'systemd_scope': bool(pre),
     'limits': '2 CPUs; RLIMIT_CPU 120 s; wall 140 s; AS 64 GiB; private RSS 6 GiB sampled; MemoryMax=6G scope if available',
     'utc_end': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime())}
(out / (label + '.receipt.json')).write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=2))
print(json.dumps({k: r[k] for k in ('label', 'exit', 'killed_reason', 'wall_seconds', 'peak_sampled_private_rss_bytes')}))
